work.author: Simeon of Beth Arsham
work.title: Letter of Simeon of Beth Arsham concerning Barsawma
work.edition: Machine translation (gpt-6.1-sol, Patristica, 2026-10-28) of: Josephus Simonius Assemani Bibliotheca Orientalis Clementino-Vaticana; TEI by J. E. Walters, Digital Syriac Corpus (syriaccorpus.org 513)

paragraphs.text: Another letter of the blessed Mar Simeon, bishop of Beth Arsham, which he wrote concerning Barsauma and the heresy of the Nestorians, showing where it originated and when it came down into the land of the Persians. For just as our true Christian faith began with Abraham, the chief of the patriarchs, through the promise that came from God, which said, “Through your offspring the nations will be blessed”—that offspring being Christ, as it is written—and through Abraham’s true faith he was called the father of all the nations, among whom we too are numbered, so too the error of the Nestorians began with Annas and Caiaphas, the chief priests, together with the rest of the Jews of that time. For those Jews considered Christ a human being, as when they said to him, “You are blaspheming, and although you are a human being, you make yourself God.” This view was being passed on by the Jews at that time. Some of them called him a human being, and some a righteous man and a prophet, a good teacher, and the king of Israel. Others, however, called him Beelzebub, the chief of the demons, a Samaritan, a blasphemer, and a transgressor of the Law. There was division among the Jews because of him. Both parties considered him a human being. This opinion is handed down among the Nestorians to this day. Simon Magus received it from those Jews. He was a Samaritan by birth, related to the Jews in certain respects, and he opposed the apostles in the city of Rome, exalting himself and saying, “I am the great one.” He considered himself the Christ, in accordance with what he had received from Annas and Caiaphas, his companions and teachers. Ebion received it from Simon, Artemon received it from Ebion, and Paul of Samosata received it from him. Paul was at one time bishop of the city of Antioch in Syria, in the days of the pagan Roman emperors, when Constantine had not yet become emperor,

the truly believing emperor of the Romans. For there was no fear of the Roman emperors. This Paul of Samosata was more brazen and blasphemed more than his teachers Simon Magus, Ebion, and Artemon. He said concerning the blessed Mary, “Mary gave birth to an ordinary human being, and she did not remain a virgin after giving birth.” He called Christ a creature, something made, and mortal, and a son by grace. He said of himself, “I too, if I wish, can become Christ, because Christ and I are of one nature.” From Paul of Samosata emerged the heresy of two natures, their individual existences, and their activities. Diodore of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, received it from Paul. From his youth he belonged to the heresy of Macedonius, who blasphemed against the Holy Spirit. When Diodore became a disciple of the Christians and became bishop of Tarsus in Cilicia, he expanded the heresy of Macedonius. He too separated the natures in Christ, their individual existences, and their activities. He considered Christ a human being, created, made, and mortal, sharing our nature, and a son by grace. In everything he followed his teacher Paul of Samosata. Theodore of Mopsuestia in Cilicia received it from Diodore. This man interpreted all the books of the Old and New Testaments. In all his interpretations and discourses, he reveals the Jewish opinion he holds concerning Christ, like his teachers Diodore and Paul of Samosata. He expanded and confirmed these teachings that came from Simon Magus, Paul, and Diodore. And a human being, created and made and mortal, sharing our nature, a son by grace, and a temple of the eternal Son. He considered Christ to be this, saying that he was not the Son of God by nature, but by grace. Along with the rest of his blasphemies, which fill all his discourses and commentaries. It was from him, Theodore, that Nestorius received these teachings. This man had been ordained a priest in the church of the great city of Antioch, and afterward became bishop of Constantinople. And there was

And he was from the city of Germanicia. He schemed to seize for himself the leadership of the wicked heresy of these teachers of his who have been mentioned above, so that all the adherents of his heresy would be called by his name, like Marcion, after whom the Marcionists were named, and like Eutyches, after whom the Eutychianists were named. For this reason Nestorius, the enemy of righteousness, openly blasphemed in the church of Constantinople. And the teachings of Simon the Magician, Ebion, Artemon, Paul of Samosata, Diodore, and Theodore—Nestorius's own teachers—had been secretly passed down among them until that time. In his arrogance, he seized for himself the leadership of the heresy. He entered and stood in the church before all the people, openly blaspheming as he said, “Do not boast, Mary, because you did not give birth to God, but to a human being, created and made and mortal, who shares our nature. Only by grace was he deemed worthy to be called the Son of God; and because of his union with mortals, Jesus is the Son of God.” Along with many other blasphemies, because of which the holy fathers in the city of Ephesus excommunicated him from the communion of the whole holy church of God, together with his teachers mentioned above, their faith, and everyone who agreed with him or with them. From that time onward, they were called Nestorians. Theodoret of Cyrrhus received these teachings from Nestorius. In his zeal on behalf of Nestorius, this Theodoret composed a wicked work against the holy fathers who had anathematized his teacher Nestorius at Ephesus. Ibas received these teachings from Theodoret. Besides all his other blasphemies, which agreed in everything with those of his teachers mentioned above, Ibas added another blasphemy in one of his discourses, saying: “I, Ibas, do not envy Christ for becoming God, for he was called God although he is a human being like me and shares my nature.” For this reason Ibas and Theodoret of Cyrrhus were anathematized, together with their associates and everyone who agreed with them. A man named Mari, from Beth Ardashir, received these teachings from Ibas. From there the land of the Persians began to be corrupted

by Nestorianism, through the letters of Ibas and the commentaries, discourses, and expositions of his teachers. After Mari, a priest from Edessa named Maron “the Fat Tail” received these teachings from Ibas. He was the scribe of the School of the Persians, which was in the city of Edessa at that time. Among the Persians who were at the school of Edessa at that time were the following: Acacius the Aramean, who was called “the Strangler of Reproaches” in that school; Barsauma, the slave of Mara the Qadruite, who was called “[?] among the Reeds”; and Mana of Beth Ardashir, who was called “the Drinker of Ashes”; and Abshuta of the city of Nineveh, who was called a name that should not be written; and John of Beth Garmai, who was called “[?].” And Micah, called Ragon, and Paul son of Qaqai, from Karka in Beth Huzaye, who was called the slave of Lubis. And Abraham the Mede, who was called Shagar-Banna, and Narsai the leper, the Azalian, from the monastery of Kfar Mari. These, together with their other companions, were united in one stubborn purpose, sharing the outlook of Ibas. There were, however, others who did not obey Ibas. Their names are written here: Mar Papa, from Beth Lapat, a city of Beth Huzaye; Mar Xenaias, from Tahal in Beth Garmai; and his brother, whose name was Addai; and Mar Barhadbshabba the Corduene, who later became abbot of the monastery of Ain Qana; and Mar Benjamin the Aramean, who later became abbot in the village of the monastery of the school, in the district of Umrin; and others with them who did not agree to the wishes of Ibas. After the death of Hisha [?], all the Persians were expelled from Edessa, together with the other Edessene scribes who agreed with them, through the efforts of the blessed Mar Cyrus, bishop of Edessa. And by the command of Zeno, emperor of the Romans, the school of [?], where they used to study, was demolished— the Persians in Edessa. In its place a church was built in the name of Lady Mary, the Mother of God. Those who had been expelled from Edessa went down to the land

of the Persians. Some of them became bishops in the cities of the Persians, namely: Acacius in Beth Aramaye; and Barsauma the swimmer in Nisibis; Mana in Beth Ardashir; John in Karka of Beth Sari in Beth Garmai; Micah in Lashom in Beth Garmai; and Paul son of Qaqai in Karka of Ledan in Beth Huzaye; and Pusai son of Qurti in Shushtar, a city of Beth Huzaye; Abraham in Beth Madaye. Narsai the leper became a teacher in Nisibis. And while the people of Beth Huzaye and the Persians were seeking the teachings of Nestorius and Theodore, just as he had received them from Ibas, he held various assemblies in the land of the Persians, first in the city of Beth Palat, the metropolis of Beth Huzaye. This took place in the twenty-seventh year of Peroz, king of kings. Then again in Seleucia-Ctesiphon, a city of Beth Aramaye, and again in the village of Beth Adrai, in the district of Beth Nuhadra. He established various canons of a new faith of their own and separated them from the true faith of the holy fathers, which they had received from the holy apostles, and which was proclaimed through the Holy Spirit in the city of Nicaea by three hundred and eighteen bishops, together with Constantine, the truly faithful emperor of the Romans. The one hundred and fifty devout and holy bishops at Constantinople also assented to it, together with Theodosius the Great, the emperor; and the two hundred and fifty-three bishops in the city of Ephesus, together with Emperor Theodosius the Younger, assented to it and confirmed it again. So too did the four hundred and ninety-five bishops of Alexandria the Great, Antioch in Syria, Cappadocia, and Galatia, together with Emperor Zeno, and in his document called the Henotikon. They also assented and confirmed it in the time of Bishop Marutha, who had been sent as an envoy by Caesar, emperor of the Romans, to Yazdegerd, king of kings, in the eleventh year of his reign, together with forty bishops from the Persian dominions. They assented to these things and confirmed them. And now also the thirty-three bishops of the land of Gurdan, together with their king and their nobles, and the thirty-two bishops of Greater Armenia

under Persian rule, together with their marzbans, along with the rest of the orthodox bishops and Christian kings, from Constantine, the truly faithful emperor, down to the blessed Emperor Anastasius, whose soul lives. All these bishops, then, each in his own time, anathematized anyone who dares to write, teach, or hand down another faith besides the one written above. This alone is held and believed by all the holy churches of the Orthodox in [?]. All the Persians held to it until the twenty-seventh year, when the Persian bishops transgressed the anathema of all the bishops and kings mentioned above. They established another faith of their own, which introduces a quaternity in addition to the Trinity, confessing the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, and Christ in two natures. For this reason we separated ourselves from communion with the Nestorians from the twenty-seventh year of King Peroz. And down to this day we have anathematized them, and we also [?] anathematize them, along with Simon the magician, their first teacher, Ebion, Artemon [?], and Paul of Samosata. And Diodore, Theodore, Nestorius, Theodoret, Ibas, and all those who followed in their footsteps and stood against the truth. Together with them and in the same way, we anathematize Mani, Marcion, Eutyches, Arius, Apollinaris, their teaching, and everyone who has thought or thinks as they do. We also fully anathematize everyone who came forward in a letter, a synod, discourses, teaching hymns, responses, or the offering of the sacrifice, or the consecration of water, or the baptismal oil, and dared to say that perfect God took from us a perfect human being for association and eternal indwelling; and everyone who makes a division and assigns divine attributes to God the Son, who is eternal, but human attributes, suffering, and death to Jesus the human being, a son by grace, and reckons two sons: one by nature and another by grace. And everyone who has spoken or speaks of two sons, their distinct individualities, and their activities in Christ after the true

and ineffable union, which truly came about from two natures. And we anathematize the faith, the canons, and everything that originated with Acacius, Barsauma [?], Narsai, and his heretical associates, and everyone who has agreed or agrees with them. We also anathematize Mari of Tahal, the teacher of Babai the catholicos. In the days of this Babai, this Mari appeared in Beth Aramaye as a teacher of the heresies of the followers of Paul of Samosata and Diodore. From him Babai the catholicos, son of Hormizd, received his teaching. He had been the secretary of Zabargan, the marzban of Beth Aramaye. Let everyone who does not confess that Mary is the Mother of God be anathema.
